task: Explain tables EKKO and EKPO to a new joiner
prompt: explain tables EKKO and EKPO to a new joiner
answer: EKKO and EKPO: Purchasing Tables in SAP EKKO and EKPO are two of the most important tables in the SAP MM (Materials Management) module. They store purchase order data. EKKO: Purchasing Document Header. One row per purchasing document (purchase order, contract, scheduling agreement). Fields: EBELN (document number), BUKRS (company code), BSART (document type), BSTYP (document category), LIFNR (vendor), EKORG (purchasing organization), EKGRP (purchasing group), AEDAT (created on), ERNAM (created by), WAERS (currency). EKPO: Purchasing Document Item. One row per item. Fields: EBELN, EBELP (item number), MATNR (material), WERKS (plant), MENGE (quantity), NETPR (net price), LOEKZ (deletion indicator). How they relate. They are linked by EBELN. One EKKO row can have many EKPO rows. Think of a paper invoice: EKKO is the top part (vendor, date) and EKPO is the list of items. Tips. Filter EKKO on BSTYP to get only purchase orders. Use SE16N to browse data. Item numbers have leading zeros, like 00010.
notes: Accurate, but about 200 words with 17 fields and no table. Too much for a new joiner who needs the keys.

prompt: Explain a real ST22 dump
answer: I need the dump text to explain a specific one. Please paste the short text and the 'Source code extract' from ST22. In general, ST22 shows ABAP runtime errors (dumps). Read these parts in order: Short text, What happened, Error analysis, How to correct the error, Source code extract. Common dumps: TIME_OUT (program ran too long), TSV_TNEW_PAGE_ALLOC_FAILED (out of memory), COMPUTE_INT_ZERODIVIDE (division by zero), SAPSQL_ARRAY_INSERT_DUPREC (duplicate key on insert).

prompt: ROLE: You are a senior SAP ABAP consultant. | TASK: Explain this ST22 dump to me. | CONTEXT: I am new to ABAP. Dump: Runtime error TSV_TNEW_PAGE_ALLOC_FAILED. Short text: No more memory available to add rows to an internal table. Program ZMM_PO_REPORT, line 142: SELECT * FROM ekpo INTO TABLE lt_ekpo. | EXAMPLES: A good answer for a different dump (COMPUTE_INT_ZERODIVIDE):  What happened: the program divided by zero. Why: the divisor field was empty. Fix: check the divisor is not 0 before dividing. | FORMAT: Four sections: What happened, Why, Where in code, How to fix. | CONSTRAINTS: Under 200 words. Simple English. Ask me if you need more of the dump.
answer: What happened: The program ZMM_PO_REPORT stopped because SAP ran out of memory. Why: Line 142 reads all of table EKPO into the internal table lt_ekpo with no filter. EKPO can hold millions of rows, so the internal table grew bigger than the memory your session is allowed to use. Where in code: Line 142: SELECT * FROM ekpo INTO TABLE lt_ekpo. How to fix: Add a WHERE condition (for example plant or date). Select only the fields you need instead of *. If you really need many rows, read them in packages with PACKAGE SIZE.
notes: Clear and correct. The fix is only described in words. No code and no way to confirm the fix worked.

prompt: ROLE: You are a senior SAP MM functional consultant. | TASK: Write the functional spec section called 'Vendor Block'. | CONTEXT: S/4HANA client. Authorizations: Only the vendor master team can set or remove blocks. Exact roles are to be defined with the security team. Test Notes: Block a test vendor, try to create a PO in ME21N and expect a message. Unblock and repeat.
notes: Solid and uses the real block fields. No assumptions or open questions, which a review meeting would ask for.
